images.title: Nine halves of a paratha
images.purpose: Show 9 pieces of 1/2 paratha joined into 4 whole parathas with 1 piece left over, and the same 9 jumps of 1/2 on a number line from 0 landing on 9/2, which is 4 1/2.
images.composition: A caption at the top, a row of 4 whole parathas cut in two and 1 half piece, then a number line from 0 to 5 with 9 jumps of 1/2 under it, and the result written large at the bottom.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TOP LEFT: the caption Baba took 9 pieces of 1/2 paratha in dark #1F2937 sans-serif (40 px), left edge at x 223, about y 50. PARATHA ROW, centred on y 200: 4 whole parathas, each a flat circle 180 px across with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px) and one thin dark vertical cut line through its centre that makes 2 equal halves; circles at x 223 to 403, 453 to 633, 683 to 863 and 913 to 1093 (gaps of 50 px); all 8 half pieces filled teal #0072B2. After a 50 px gap, 1 half paratha, a flat semicircle 90 px wide and 180 px high (x 1143 to 1233, its straight edge at the left, the curve at the right) filled reddish purple #CC79A7 with the same outline. Under the 4 circles a thin grey #6B7280 bracket line (x 223 to 1093, y 310) with the text 4 whole parathas centred under it (36 px, about y 350); under the semicircle the text 1/2 left over (36 px, about y 350). So 9 half pieces in all, 8 teal and 1 purple. NUMBER LINE: one thin dark horizontal line at y 560 from x 153 to x 1303, with exactly 11 vertical tick marks, one every 115 px from x 153 to x 1303: 6 tall ticks (44 px) at x 153, 383, 613, 843, 1073 and 1303, labelled under the line 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 (44 px, bold, dark, about y 625), and 5 short ticks (26 px) between them at x 268, 498, 728, 958 and 1188 with no labels. JUMPS: exactly 9 curved arrows, each starting on one tick and ending on the next tick to its right (each 115 px wide and about 55 px high, arrowhead at the right end), the first starting at 0 and the 9th ending at 4 1/2: the first 8 arrows teal and the 9th arrow (x 1073 to 1188) reddish purple. A reddish purple dot (24 px) on the line at x 1188 with the label 9/2 above the 9th arrow (56 px, bold, dark, about y 440). Across the bottom centre, about y 735, one line of bold dark text, 9/2 = 4 1/2 (80 px), the largest text in the frame. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 9 half pieces, 9 arrows or 11 tick marks
a number label on any tick other than 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5
images.takeaway: 9 pieces of 1/2 make 4 whole parathas and 1 half left over, so 9/2 = 4 1/2.
images.description: Four whole parathas cut in two and one half piece, with a number line from 0 to 5 showing 9 jumps of 1/2 that land on 9/2, and 9/2 = 4 1/2 written below.
images.context: Concept image for Halves Make Parathas (fractions greater than 1). It follows the idea of the figures in your maths book (pieces of 1/2 paratha joined two at a time, and halves placed along a number line) and shows the concept's own example of 9 pieces of 1/2.
images.teaching_notes: Join the pieces two at a time with the child: 4 pairs make 4 whole parathas and 1 piece stays alone. The slip to watch is reading 4 1/2 as 4 times 1/2: it is 4 whole parathas and 1/2 more.

image_decisions.why: The 9 half pieces joined into whole parathas and the 9 jumps on the number line show the same total two ways.
